newsitem.title: USA: AIDS activists strew ashes near White House.
newsitem.headline: AIDS activists strew ashes near White House.

text.p: A demonstration by 300 gay rights activists was dispersed Sunday by U.S. Park Police after the protesters threw what they said were human ashes on the sidewalk in front of the White House, according to police and local media reports.
Park Police spokesman John Loveland said the sidewalk in front of the executive mansion was shut for about 40 minutes Sunday afternoon after the incident.
Loveland said the protesters threw plastic bags filled with ashes, but could not confirm whether they were of human origin.

Calling for increased funding to battle AIDS, members of the group ACT UP marched to the White House after reviewing the 40,000 panels of the AIDS Memorial Quilt, on display at the Great Mall and stretching from the Capitol to the Washington Monument.
